headline: Pyridostigmine
punch: It doubled the GH response to exercise.

headline: There is a drug that lowers it
subhead: AND IT IS OLD AND BORING
body: So if somatostatin is the brake, the obvious question is whether anything takes it off. There is, it has been in use for decades, and it is not a peptide anyone is selling you. | Pyridostigmine is a cholinesterase inhibitor, meaning it stops acetylcholine being broken down. Cholinergic tone is one of the inputs that lowers hypothalamic somatostatin, which is why this unremarkable old drug ended up as a standard research tool for probing the GH axis.

headline: What does it do to exercise GH?
subhead: WHAT IT DID TO EXERCISE GH
body: Nine healthy volunteers, measured twice. Exercise on its own produced a GH area under the curve of **292.6**. The same exercise after pyridostigmine produced **587.3**, at P < 0.005. | Peak GH went from 6.5 to **13.5 µg/l**, P < 0.01. What this means is that the same physical session, in the same people, produced roughly double the growth hormone purely because the brake had been eased beforehand.

headline: Additive, not synergistic
body: The authors did the arithmetic that most studies skip. The action of pyridostigmine was **additive** to exercise, because the sum of the two separate responses was not significantly different from the combined response. | That distinction matters when you are reasoning about stacking anything. It behaved like a second independent input arriving alongside the first, not like a multiplier that makes the first one bigger. Two things adding up, not one amplifying the other.
punch: Two inputs stacking, not one amplifying the other.

headline: Spoudeas 1992
body: This is the one nobody quotes and it changes what you would do with the drug. They gave two GHRH stimuli 90 minutes apart on a pyridostigmine background and measured both. | Pyridostigmine **enhanced the first GH response**, with an increased rate of GH release. And the **second GH responses were not augmented**. The first pulse got bigger and the second pulse got nothing, on the same background, in the same session.
punch: ==It worked on the first pulse. Not the second.==

headline: Read that again
body: If the cholinergic lever only improves the pulse it happens to be timed to, then taking it repeatedly through the day is not purchasing repeated benefit. You are paying for one improved window and getting billed for several. | The honest version is that it opens one good window. What you choose to put in that window is the actual decision, and the number of times you dose is not the variable people think it is.

headline: Can it rescue an older axis?
body: They ran it in young and old men during exercise. It raised the GH area under the curve during maximal exercise, **20.9 against 4.9**, and during submaximal exercise, **12.3 against 4.7**, both at P < 0.05. Real and large in both age groups. | But it **failed to restore the responses of the old to those of the young**. Their conclusion was that increased somatostatin tone does not completely explain the age difference in GH secretion. Something else is also wrong, and lifting the brake does not fix it.
punch: It lifts the brake. It does not rebuild the engine.

headline: It is not the only route
body: Arginine lowers somatostatin tone as well, which is exactly why the arginine plus GHRH test is a standard clinical probe of GH reserve in humans. Same gate, different door, and a much older method. | So the cholinergic lever is one of several ways onto the same control point rather than a unique mechanism, and that is worth knowing before anyone treats pyridostigmine as something special rather than as one option among several.
punch: The gate has more than one door.

headline: What this actually is
body: Every human study quoted here uses pyridostigmine as a **research probe**, to ask how much somatostatin is currently holding GH down in a given person. That is what the pyridostigmine test is for and that is why these experiments exist. | It is not studied as a growth protocol, no dose here is a recommendation, and the gap between an established mechanism and a tested application is the whole distance between those two things.
punch: ==The mechanism is solid. The application is not studied.==
